blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Long-video question answering benchmarks like Video-MME-v2 typically evaluate systems under a uniform frame budget for every question, despite stark variation in the evidence each query actually demands. We analyze this mismatch on Video-MME-v2 and find that different question subsets prefer different frozen frame-budget policies, while uniformly increasing the frame count does not reliably improve all metrics. These findings motivate fixed-mean frame-budget routing, a controlled inference setting in which each question may receive a different frame budget while the average budget matches a uniform reference. We introduce FrameRouter, a training-free test-time framework that combines an evidence-demand router, a budget-constrained allocation rule, and a frozen bank of frame-sampling policies. By controlling how much visual evidence each question receives while leaving the underlying samplers unchanged, FrameRouter is orthogonal to query-aware frame selection. Across Video-MME-v2 and several long-video understanding benchmarks, FrameRouter improves long-video question answering by using the same average visual budget more selectively across questions. Code is available at https://github.com/bingjunluo/FrameRouter.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Long-video question answering has become a stress test for multimodal models:
the system must search, aggregate, and reason over visual evidence spread
across minutes or hours of video. Recent benchmarks such as Video-MME-v2,
MLVU, and LongVideoBench make this pressure explicit by evaluating models
across long durations, diverse domains, subtitles, and multi-step question
groups ( Fu et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) .
Because compute and context length restrict the number of frames that current
video–language models can ingest, frame budget has become a central evaluation
knob. The de facto protocol is to fix a uniform per-question budget and apply
it to every instance. This is simple and reproducible, but it tacitly assumes
that every question deserves the same amount of visual evidence.

blocks.en:
That assumption sits uneasily with the structure of modern long-video
benchmarks. Their questions span heterogeneous evidence demands: some are
resolvable from sparse global context, scene-level commonsense, or subtitle
cues, while others hinge on local visual details, long-range temporal
association, action ordering, or repeated-action counting. Spending the same
number of frames on every question therefore creates two coupled
inefficiencies: low-demand questions consume frames they may not need, and
high-demand questions remain under-observed. Recent efficient video-QA work
makes a related observation, showing that uniformly sampled long videos
contain substantial redundancy and that question-aware frame selection can
recover crucial spatiotemporal cues ( Park et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Yao et al., 2025 ; Ben-Ami et al., 2026 ) . Our focus is orthogonal to which frames a
question keeps: we ask how much evidence each question should receive under
the same average cost.

blocks.en:
We instantiate this formulation as FrameRouter , a training-free
test-time framework that routes frame budgets , not frame locations.
FrameRouter scores the benchmark question prompt, whose multiple-choice
options are visible to any evaluated system, and uses those question-only
priorities to choose among frozen low-, mid-, and high-budget full-video
policies under an exact dataset-level mean-budget constraint. The router never
sees the video, subtitles, sibling questions, other videos, labels, or
candidate policy outputs, and it neither fine-tunes the underlying VLM nor
introduces a new within-question frame selector. This keeps the comparison
tightly controlled: low- and high-budget assignments change the distribution
of visual evidence across questions, while the average number of frames remains
identical to the uniform reference. Across Video-MME-v2, LongVideoBench,
MVBench, and VideoMMMU, FrameRouter yields stable matched-budget improvements.
Quota sweeps and post-hoc route audits further show that the benefit is not
simply a high-budget effect, but comes from reallocating the fixed average
budget across heterogeneous questions.

blocks.en:
In summary, our contributions are threefold as follows: • We diagnose non-monotonic frame-budget effects on Video-MME-v2 and
formalize fixed-mean frame-budget routing as a controlled inference problem,
separating dataset-level budget reallocation from variable-frame efficiency
and from within-question frame selection. • We instantiate this problem as FrameRouter, combining a frozen
full-video uniform policy bank, a question-only evidence-demand priority
parser, and a quota-constrained allocator that holds the mean frame budget
exactly equal to the uniform reference. • We achieve the state-of-the-art open-source result on
Video-MME-v2 under the matched-budget protocol, and show consistent
improvements across other benchmarks, including LongVideoBench, MVBench, and VideoMMMU.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Long-video understanding benchmarks
blocks.zh: 2.1 长视频理解基准

blocks.en:
Long-video understanding has moved from short, isolated clips toward benchmarks
that require models to integrate evidence over minutes or hours. EgoSchema
introduced a diagnostic multiple-choice setting over three-minute egocentric
clips, emphasizing that temporal difficulty is not captured by clip length
alone ( Mangalam et al., 2023 ) . Video-MME broadened evaluation across video
duration, domain, and modality, including subtitles and audio, and exposed a
large gap between frontier proprietary systems and open models on long-video
analysis ( Fu et al., 2025 ) . MLVU and LongVideoBench further expanded the
evaluation surface with multi-task long-video understanding and interleaved
video-language contexts ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) . These
benchmarks made frame budget a practical evaluation variable: model quality
depends not only on the backbone, but also on how many frames or visual tokens
are admitted into the context.

blocks.en:
Video-MME-v2 sharpens this pressure by changing both the data distribution and
the scoring rule ( Fu et al., 2026 ) . It contains 800 recent videos and
3,200 questions, organized into groups of four interrelated questions. Beyond
average per-question accuracy, the benchmark reports group-level non-linear
scores, including Non-Lin, Consistency, and Coherence, that reward models for
answering related questions consistently and for preserving multi-step reasoning
chains within a group. These metrics matter for budgeted inference because the
same video can contain questions with very different evidence demands: global
story context, long-range temporal aggregation, local perceptual details, OCR,
or screen evidence. A uniform frame budget is therefore poorly matched to the
heterogeneity that Video-MME-v2 is well suited to surfacing.

blocks.en: 2.2 Efficient video question answering
blocks.zh: 2.2 高效的视频问答

blocks.en:
The high cost of video QA has motivated methods that reduce redundant visual
processing. Early long-video QA systems often uniformly sampled many frames and
converted them into captions or visual tokens, but long videos contain large
regions that are irrelevant to a particular question. As models and benchmarks
move to longer inputs, evaluation quality depends not only on the VLM backbone
but also on frame budget, sampling density, and whether auxiliary channels such
as subtitles or interleaved text are admitted into the context. The official
64-frame-with-subtitle setting in Video-MME-v2 makes this cost–accuracy
tradeoff explicit: more evidence can help difficult questions, but increasing
the per-question budget uniformly also spends frames on questions that may not
need them.

blocks.en:
Existing efficient video-QA methods mostly reduce the cost of processing each
question. LVNet explicitly argues that many sampled frames are unnecessary and
uses a hierarchical keyframe selector to reduce the captioning burden for
long-form QA ( Park et al., 2026 ) . Agentic approaches such as VideoAgent ask an
LLM controller to iteratively search for useful visual information under a
limited frame budget ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . Architecture-level approaches
also attack the cost problem by compressing the video representation: MA-LMM
maintains a memory bank for long-term video information ( He et al., 2024 ) ,
while LongVU uses spatiotemporal adaptive compression to reduce token redundancy
while preserving salient visual detail ( Shen et al., 2024 ) . These works
establish that long-video QA is governed by a cost–accuracy tradeoff, but their
primary unit of adaptation is usually the video, the segment, or the selected
frame set for a single query.

blocks.en: 2.3 Adaptive visual evidence and test-time compute

blocks.en:
Most recent efficient video-LLM methods adapt which visual evidence is
shown to the model, while a broader adaptive-compute literature studies
inference-time allocation more generally. Query-aware frame selection methods
score frames by their relevance to the current question, often combining
temporal coverage with visual-textual matching. Q-Frame selects frames and
adapts resolution according to the video content and query ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) ;
GenS trains a generative frame sampler under capped frame budgets ( Yao et al., 2025 ) ;
and HiMu composes expert grounding signals for hierarchical frame
selection ( Ben-Ami et al., 2026 ) . In language-model serving and conditional
computation, FrugalGPT uses query-dependent cascades to reduce cost ( Chen et al., 2023 ) ,
RouteLLM routes between stronger and weaker LLMs as a cost-quality
tradeoff ( Ong et al., 2024 ) , and Mixture-of-Depths allocates transformer
computation dynamically across tokens ( Raposo et al., 2024 ) .
Input-dependent mixture-of-experts routing has likewise been adopted beyond language modeling ( Xi et al., 2025 ) .
These works
share the premise that uniform computation is wasteful when inputs have
heterogeneous difficulty.

Our work connects these two perspectives in long-video QA. Rather than learning
a new retriever, selecting timestamps, or routing between different models,
FrameRouter reallocates a fixed dataset-level frame budget across questions
using frozen VLM inference configurations. Thus it is complementary to
within-question frame selection: those methods ask which evidence to keep,
whereas we ask how much visual evidence each question should receive under the
same average budget.

问题框内选择 : 这些方法要求哪些证据可以保存,

blocks.en: 3 Analysis: why route frame budgets?

We argue that uniform frame budgets are a poor unit of comparison on

without conflating budget allocation with other design choices, we analyze a frozen policy bank of three full-video uniform sampling policies: low,

blocks.en: 3.3 From diagnostics to design

blocks.en:
These diagnostics suggest a narrow design space for a deployable router. To
isolate budget allocation from frame-selection effects, the route should choose
among the frozen full-video policies in Π \Pi rather than introduce a new
sampler or temporal localizer. To avoid test-time leakage, the routing signal
should be computed from the current question prompt only, excluding labels,
videos, subtitles, sibling questions, other videos, model answers, and policy
outcomes. Because the route cannot observe which policy will be correct, the
signal should be an interpretable prior over evidence demand rather than a
direct correctness predictor. Finally, comparisons must enforce the same
dataset-level mean frame budget as the uniform reference; higher means are
separate operating points.

blocks.en: 5.1 Setup
blocks.zh: 5.1 设置

blocks.en: We evaluate on four video understanding benchmarks: Video-MME-v2 ( Fu et al., 2026 ) , LongVideoBench ( Wu et al., 2024 ) , MVBench ( Li et al., 2024 ) , and VideoMMMU ( Hu et al., 2025 ) . Video-MME-v2 provides the most detailed protocol for our main analysis: in addition to average accuracy, it reports official group-level scores for non-linear reasoning, three difficulty levels, consistency, and coherence, and we evaluate both subtitle and no-subtitle settings. LongVideoBench is also evaluated in both subtitle settings, while MVBench and VideoMMMU are evaluated with their official accuracy metrics. Unless otherwise noted, all reported numbers follow the corresponding benchmark evaluation protocol.
blocks.zh: 我们评价了四个视频理解基准:Video-MME-v2(Fu等,2026年),LongVideo Bench(Wu等,2024年),MV Bench(Li等,2024年)和VideoMMU(Hu等,2025年). Video-MME-v2为我们的主要分析提供了最详细的协议:除了平均准确性外,它还报告非线性推理,三个难度级,一致性,和一致性的官方组级分数,我们同时评价字幕和无子标题设置. LongVideo Bench也在两个字幕设置中受到评价,而MV Bench和VideoMMU则以官方的准确度衡量标准受到评价. 除非另有说明,所有报告的数字都遵循相应的基准评价协议。

blocks.en: Our controlled baseline is uniform mid-budget inference with the same Qwen3.5-397B-A17B backbone ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) . We evaluate both Instruct and Think regimes, and constrain FrameRouter to the same average visual frame budget using the frozen 48/64/96 full-video policy bank. The parser is a deterministic text-only call to the same model used by the answer-stage VLM, which receives only question/options, processes no video frames, and is capped at 160 output tokens, so its overhead is negligible compared with the heavy multimodal answer call over 48/64/96 frames and up to 1024 generated tokens. For context, we also include frontier commercial systems such as Gemini-3-Pro ( Google DeepMind, 2025 ) , GPT-5 ( OpenAI, 2026 ) , and Kimi-K2.5 ( Kimi Team, 2026 ) , together with open-source video LMMs such as Qwen3-VL ( Bai et al., 2025a ) , LLaVA-Video ( Zhang et al., 2024 ) , InternVL3.5 ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , and Qwen2.5-VL ( Bai et al., 2025b ) .
blocks.zh: 我们的控制基线是统一的中预算推论,与同为Quen3.5-397B-A17B的主干线(Quen Team, 2026. 我们利用被冻结的48/64/96全视频政策库,评估指令和思维制度,并将Frame Router限制在相同的平均视觉框架预算。 解析器是针对解析阶段VLM所使用的同一种模式的定型文本只调用,它只接收出问题/选项,不处理视频帧,并被封顶为160个出品符,因此与48/64/96帧以上的重多式解析调用相比,其间接费用可忽略不计,最多可有1024个生成符. 在背景方面,我们还包括了双子座-3-Pro(Google DeepMind,2025年),GPT-5(OpenAI,2026年)和Kimi-K2.5(Kimi Team,2026年)等前沿商业系统,以及开源视频LMM,如Qune3-VL(Bai等,2025a年),LLAVA-Video(张等,2024年),InternVL3.5(Wang等,2025年)和Quen2.5-VL(Bai等,2025b年)等.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
This work studies whether a uniform per-question frame budget is the best use
of a fixed average visual budget for long-video question answering. Our
diagnostics on Video-MME-v2 show that nearby frame budgets help different
question subsets, motivating fixed-mean frame-budget routing as a controlled
test-time setting. FrameRouter instantiates this setting with a training-free
question-only evidence-demand parser and a quota-constrained allocator over a
frozen bank of full-video uniform policies. Across Video-MME-v2,
LongVideoBench, MVBench, and VideoMMMU, the results show that matched-budget
gains can be obtained by reallocating visual evidence across heterogeneous
questions rather than increasing the average frame count. Budget routing is
therefore a simple inference axis complementary to frame selection, token
compression, and model scaling.

blocks.zh: A.2 解析器证据锁定剖面

blocks.en:
Section 5.4 reports how the final routes
distribute across official group × \times level splits. The diagnostic below
looks at the same routed questions from the parser side. During routing, the
question-only parser emits an evidence-anchor category together with its
low- and high-budget priorities. These categories are not used as ground-truth
annotations and are not meant to localize evidence in the video; they are
self-reported parser fields that help interpret why different questions are
assigned to different budget routes. We aggregate these anchor categories
within each final route to check whether the route assignments correspond to
coherent evidence-demand profiles.

blocks.en:
This analysis should be read as an interpretability check rather than as an
additional source of supervision. The allocator consumes only the two priority
scores described in Section 4.3 ; the evidence-anchor field
is logged for auditing and is not used to choose the route. A meaningful
anchor–route association is therefore useful because it shows that the parser
priorities are not arbitrary scalar scores: they are accompanied by stable,
human-readable evidence profiles that align with the intended roles of the low,
mid, and high routes.

blocks.en:
Figure 5 gives a parser-side view
of the realized routes. The high route is strongly enriched for temporal
evidence-anchor outputs, while the low route contains more uncertain,
local-visual, and subtitle-oriented profiles. The mid route remains more mixed,
consistent with its role as the fallback route when neither compression nor
promotion is strongly preferred. These anchors are not human annotations and do
not imply temporal localization, but they help verify that the question-only
parser induces interpretable route structure rather than an arbitrary budget
mixture.

blocks.en:
This section summarizes implementation details of our method. The default configuration matches the main
Video-MME-v2 Think-with-subtitles setting unless otherwise specified.

blocks.en:
FrameRouter uses a three-policy full-video uniform bank with low, mid, and
high budgets set to 48, 64, and 96 frames, respectively. For the 48/64/96 bank this gives twice as many
low routes as high routes. Parser and answer calls use temperature 0.0 0.0 by default. The parser response
length is 160 tokens, while the answer response length is 1024 tokens.

高预算分别为48、64和96个框架。 对于48/64/96银行来说,这给两倍
低道为高道. 解析和接听电话默认使用温度为0.0. 解析器响应
长度为160个令牌,而答案响应长度为1024个令牌.

blocks.en:
The parser returns priority_48 , priority_96 , confidence , evidence_anchor , and a short rationale. Scores
are clamped to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , and malformed or missing scores default to conservative
mid-range values. The allocator first selects the high route by descending priority_96 , then selects the low route from the remaining questions
by descending priority_48 ; all remaining questions use the mid route.
Ties are broken by a deterministic hash of the dataset index, and the code
raises an error if the allocated mean frame count differs from the mid-budget
target. The answer stage then runs only the selected route for each question,
using uniform sampling and the baseline Video-MME-v2 prompt layout inherited
from the evaluation script.

The released parser prompt is presented below. The prompt explicitly states
the information boundary of the router, the fixed-mean budget setting, the
semantics of the two priority scores, and the required JSON output format.

blocks.en: You are a text-only priority router for long-video multiple-choice QA. You cannot see the video and you do not know the answer. Use only the current question and answer options. Do not answer the question. Do not use labels, sibling questions, other videos, or dataset statistics. A strict solver will keep the average budget fixed at 64 frames: - a small top group by priority_96 will use 96 frames; - twice as many questions by priority_48 will use 48 frames; - all remaining questions will use the default 64 frames. Your job is to output the two final ranking priorities directly. Do not output a weighted formula; do not choose the number of questions assigned to each budget. priority_48 should be high only when reducing 64f to 48f is likely safe: - the decisive evidence is local, static, repeated, or easy to locate; - 64f looks more than sufficient from the question/options; - the question is anchored by a clear subtitle/dialogue/text/object cue; - no broad temporal coverage, counting, order tracking, or subtle multi-scene comparison is needed. priority_96 should be high only when extra frames are likely useful: - subtitle/dialogue/text anchoring is weak or absent; - the decisive visual evidence is hard to localize from text alone; - broad temporal coverage, counting, event order, changes, or repeated actions are central; - the options require fine visual discrimination across moments. Important calibration: - Most questions should remain 64f, so both priorities should often be modest. - Do not make priority_96 high merely because the question seems hard; extra frames only help when the missing evidence is temporal/visual coverage. - Do not make priority_48 high for OCR, tiny text, rare brief details, or fine visual distinctions even if the evidence is local. - If unsure, set both priorities near 0.40-0.55 and confidence below 0.60. Return compact JSON only: { "policy": "DEFAULT_64F", "priority_48": 0.00, "priority_96": 0.00, "confidence": 0.00, "evidence_anchor": "subtitle|visual_local|visual_broad|temporal|mixed|uncertain", "rationale": "<=10 words" } Question: {question} Options: {options}
blocks.zh: 您是长视频多选择QA的文本优先路由器 。 你看不到视频,也不知道答案。 只使用当前问答选项 。 不要回答这个问题。 不要使用标签、兄弟间问题、其他视频或数据集统计。 严格的解答器会将平均预算固定在64帧: - 按优先级_96排列的一小组顶级组会使用96帧; - 按优先级_48排列的提问数量将两倍于48帧; - 所有剩余问题都将使用默认的64帧. 你的工作是直接输出最后两个优先级 不输出加权公式;不选择分配给每个预算的问题数量。 只有当将64f减少到48f 时,才应是高的: - 决定性证据是局部的,静态的,重复的,或易于找到的; - 64f 从问题/选项来看,看起来已经足够了; - 问题以明确的字幕/对话/文本/对象提示为主; - 不需要广泛的时间覆盖、计数、跟踪命令或微妙的多场比较。 优先级_96 只有在额外框架可能有用时才应很高: - 字幕/对话/文本锁定薄弱或缺失; - 决定性的视觉证据难以从文本中本地化; - 广泛的时间覆盖、计数、事件顺序、变化或重复行动是中心; - 选项需要瞬间细微的视觉歧视。 重要的校准: - 大多数问题仍应保留为64f,因此这两个优先事项往往应适度。 不要仅仅因为问题看起来很困难而高优先级_96;额外框架只有在缺失的证据是时间/视觉覆盖时才有用。 不要让优先权_48 对OCR,微小的文本,稀有的简短细节,或细微的视觉区别,即使证据是局部的. - 如果不确定,则确定优先顺序接近0.40-0.55,信心低于0.60。 返回 Contract JSON 只: {"政策":"DEFAULT_64F","优先"-48":0.00 "优先"-96":"自信":0.00 "证据":"subtititle_visual_local_visual_broad_timporal_mixed_unconfirm","理由":"<="-10个字"}问:{问题} 选项 : {选项}

blocks.en:
The code implementation of FrameRouter is publicly available at https://github.com/bingjunluo/FrameRouter . The code is organized to match the method contract in
Section 4.2 : the router first reads only the current
question and its answer options, assigns one frame budget, and then runs
exactly one selected full-video uniform policy. It does not inspect video
frames, subtitles, labels, sibling questions, other videos, or any
candidate-policy outputs before route assignment. The released pipeline
therefore implements the deployable path used in the paper rather than a
post-hoc selector that runs multiple answer policies and chooses among their
outputs.

The entry point is run_framerouter.py , with command-line arguments
defined in framerouter/cli.py . Runtime and frame-budget settings are
kept in framerouter/config.py . The question-only routing prompt is in framerouter/router_prompt.py , while framerouter/router.py performs the parser call, JSON extraction, and
parser TSV normalization. The deterministic fixed-mean budget assignment is
implemented in framerouter/allocation.py . After allocation, framerouter/policy.py runs the selected 48/64/96-frame Video-MME-v2
inference policy, and framerouter/scoring.py wraps Video-MME-v2
scoring. The end-to-end orchestration lives in framerouter/pipeline.py ; run_videommev2.sh provides an
example command for the main Video-MME-v2 setting.

blocks.en:
The paper experiments were run on an 8 × \times NVIDIA H200 server using vLLM
with the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API and a Python 3.10+ client. The
inputs are Video-MME-v2 parquet metadata, extracted video files, and subtitle
JSONL files. Frames may be transported as base64-encoded JPEGs or through local
media paths supported by the inference server. The implementation is otherwise
model-server agnostic as long as the server accepts OpenAI-compatible
multimodal chat-completions requests.

JSONL档案. 框架可作为基质64-编码JPEG或通过本地
由推断服务器支持的媒体路径。 执行则不然
